name: six
remediation_notes: Python 2 support ended in 2020. Migrate away by replacing each six utility with its Python 3 equivalent: `six.string_types` → `str`, `six.moves.urllib` → `urllib`, etc.

name: pytz
remediation_notes: For Python 3.9+, migrate to stdlib zoneinfo with the tzdata package. Dormant (last release 2022) but showing recent commits. Older projects should pin versions and plan upgrades.

name: itsdangerous
remediation_notes: Itsdangerous is stable and broadly depended on with no single steward. Most projects should pin the version and monitor for security updates rather than attempting a costly migration.

name: colorama
remediation_notes: Colorama is dormant but stable; it does one thing well and the maintainers are transparently conservative about changes. Most projects can safely pin the current version. Only switch to Rich if you need advanced terminal formatting features beyond basic colors.

name: mccabe
remediation_notes: mccabe is a complete, stable complexity checker; dormancy reflects finished work rather than abandonment. Pin the version, use as-is. Alternatives (radon, pylint) require config changes across projects and aren't drop-in replacements.

name: py
remediation_notes: Explicitly in maintenance mode with clear deprecation guidance per README. Components have moved to alternatives: py.path→pathlib, py.apipkg→apipkg, py.iniconfig→iniconfig, py.code→pytest. Dependent must identify which slice it uses and migrate to the corresponding package.

name: decorator
remediation_notes: Small, dependency-free codebase—safe to pin. Python's functools has evolved to cover many use cases, but individual migration to functools or wrapt is low-priority given the ecosystem scale.

name: toml
remediation_notes: tomli is actively maintained and TOML 1.0 compliant, providing a drop-in replacement for most use cases. Python 3.11+ projects needing only read access can use the built-in tomllib instead.

name: traitlets
remediation_notes: Traitlets powers Jupyter's configuration layer and is maintained minimally by that ecosystem. Dependents should pin versions; replacing it requires leaving Jupyter or piecemeal switching to attrs/Pydantic if not deeply integrated.

name: cycler
remediation_notes: Stable utility with zero runtime dependencies, dormant but not broken; 98K dependents largely indirect through matplotlib. Pinning the version is the appropriate mitigation.

name: pickleshare
remediation_notes: Pickleshare is 530 lines with no runtime dependencies—copy it into your project rather than depend on the dormant package.

name: requests-oauthlib
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 2+ years, zero active maintainers. Migrate OAuth 2 workflows to authlib (which maintains both 1 & 2); OAuth 1-specific use may require partial vendoring or pinning.

name: defusedxml
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable and widely relied upon (94K dependents). Pin to a known-good version and monitor for new CVE reports.

name: pexpect
remediation_notes: Pexpect is broadly adopted but dormant with no maintained alternative. Dependents should evaluate their specific subprocess control requirements and migrate to targeted solutions: subprocess for basic spawning, paramiko for SSH, or fork for full expect-like interactivity.

name: ptyprocess
remediation_notes: Stable dormant code with 84K dependents and no transitive issues; pty handling is focused and unchanged. Pin the version and accept the slow-update risk rather than force migration.

name: mock
remediation_notes: This is a backport of unittest.mock, which is part of Python's standard library (3.3+). Migrate to the built-in version instead of maintaining a dependency on this dormant package.

name: webencodings
remediation_notes: Stable WHATWG encoding standard implementation; 1,161 lines with zero dependencies makes vendoring a practical low-risk path for consumers.

name: future
remediation_notes: Python 2 reached end-of-life in 2020. The maintainers explicitly recommend against new dependencies. If you still support Python 2, pin to a stable old version and plan to remove it as you end Python 2 compatibility. Otherwise, drop the dependency and update code to Python 3-only.

name: backcall
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for six years but has zero runtime dependencies and a stable, straightforward 1.3k-LOC codebase. Pinning the version carries minimal risk. Vendoring is viable if concerns arise.

name: entrypoints
remediation_notes: Package explicitly recommends migrating to stdlib importlib.metadata (3.8+) or importlib-metadata backport. Dormant since 2017; functionality now built into Python standard library.

name: mypy-extensions
remediation_notes: Small focused typing library with stable dormancy; common pattern for mature type-system utilities. Pin versions and monitor for security reports.

name: appdirs
remediation_notes: Officially deprecated since 2017 with zero maintenance activity. Maintainers recommend switching to platformdirs, their actively maintained successor.

name: pyasn1-modules
remediation_notes: Dormant since mid-2024 but stable. Pin the version and monitor Python compatibility. Large projects critical to infrastructure could fork or migrate ASN.1-dependent code to the cryptography library for new work.

name: rsa
remediation_notes: Archived with maintainer explicitly refusing handover due to security risk. The cryptography library is actively maintained and handles RSA operations; test API compatibility before migrating.

name: seaborn
remediation_notes: Seaborn is mature visualization code with stable dependencies and no viable drop-in replacement at this scale. Pin to a recent release and accept the dormancy; wholesale switching (plotly, altair, etc.) would require API rewrites across thousands of projects.

name: nbformat
remediation_notes: nbformat is the reference Python implementation of the Jupyter Notebook format and remains actively maintained by the Jupyter project. Dormancy reflects format stability, not abandonment. Dependents should pin the version and accept this well-known, stable dependency.

name: terminado
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable; primarily used by Jupyter projects. No security issues or dead transitive dependencies. Pin the version and intervene only if a specific issue emerges.

name: pandocfilters
remediation_notes: panflute is actively maintained and recommended in pandocfilters' README as the more Pythonic alternative. It accounts for 93% of dependent usage; upgrade direct users to panflute.

name: google-auth
remediation_notes: Repository archived by Google with code consolidated into google-cloud-python. This is the official maintained location; dependents should migrate there for ongoing updates.

name: sniffio
remediation_notes: No maintained alternative exists for detecting which async runtime is active. Pin the version and accept the dormancy risk; monitor for Python compatibility issues on version releases.

name: async-timeout
remediation_notes: The library is explicitly deprecated and upstreamed into Python 3.11's asyncio.Timeout. Dependents should use conditional imports to support both old and new Python versions, then drop the dependency once Python <3.11 support ends.

name: html5lib
remediation_notes: html5lib is a stable, spec-compliant HTML5 parser relied on by 46k+ repos with varying needs. Projects using it for lenient HTML parsing can migrate to lxml or stdlib, but those requiring WHATWG compliance have limited alternatives; some may need to fork or accept the maintenance risk.

name: blinker
remediation_notes: Blinker is a 322-LOC signal dispatcher with zero runtime dependencies—a solved problem that doesn't require active development. The Pallets Community Ecosystem backing and 2 active maintainers suggest organizational stability. Pin to a stable version.

name: argparse
remediation_notes: argparse is in the Python standard library for all supported versions (2.7+, 3.2+); replace the dead PyPI dependency with the stdlib module

name: h11
remediation_notes: h11 is dormant (369 days) with an unresolved advisory. Migrate to httpcore, which is actively maintained and provides the same HTTP/1.1 protocol handling the h11 ecosystem was built on.

name: alabaster
remediation_notes: Alabaster is the default Sphinx theme but unmaintained since 641 days. Switch to an actively maintained alternative like furo or pydata-sphinx-theme, which are drop-in replacements.

name: asn1crypto
remediation_notes: Pure-Python ASN.1 library with no dependencies and stable codebase; 81.6% of use concentrated in pyaxmlparser. Version pinning is appropriate—breaking changes unlikely.

name: text-unidecode
remediation_notes: Python-slugify drives all usage (75M+ downloads). At 16 lines with zero dependencies, easily replaceable. The README names unidecode as the maintained alternative with better memory and transliteration.

name: inflection
remediation_notes: String inflection is stable, mature functionality—most dependents should vendor the small codebase (1026 LOC) rather than coordinate an ecosystem-wide migration.

name: nest-asyncio
remediation_notes: Scattered across 28k repos with no unified steward or maintained alternative. The core patch is minimal (351 LOC) with no dependencies; pinning a stable version spreads less maintenance burden than vendoring across 639 packages or requiring architectural refactors.

name: tzlocal
remediation_notes: tzlocal fills a niche that standard library zoneinfo doesn't fully address. Small (2K LOC), zero runtime deps, stable code despite dormancy. Pin version and monitor for critical issues.

name: gitdb
remediation_notes: Mature library in dormant maintenance. No breaking issues in recent history. Primary use through GitPython; direct users should pin versions and monitor for security updates.

name: smmap
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable memory-mapping library with small, focused codebase and no transitive issues. No drop-in replacement exists; Python's built-in mmap lacks the resource management and LRU eviction this provides. Pin versions and fork if modifications are needed.

name: pure-eval
remediation_notes: Stack-data (130M downloads) dominates all dependents; essentially all 24k repos reach pure-eval transitively. The IPython/Jupyter ecosystem should fork this 1.5K-line, stable, dependency-free codebase to guarantee maintenance within their governance.

name: stack-data
remediation_notes: Stack-data is stable, specialized code for extracting stack frame data. No maintained alternative exists; the standard library doesn't provide this. Pin the version and accept the dormant status.

name: google-pasta
remediation_notes: TensorFlow variants account for 90% of usage; this is effectively Google's library. They should fork it or migrate to libcst. For others, follow TensorFlow's lead.

name: sortedcontainers
remediation_notes: Pure Python sorted collections with zero runtime dependencies; 3.2K lines of stable code is simple to vendor locally. The 23.7K dependent repos should copy this in rather than rely on unmaintained releases.

name: requests-toolbelt
remediation_notes: Spans multipart encoding, SSL adapters, and helpers; each has alternatives (urllib3/httpx, stdlib ssl, inline code). Dormant 3+ years; different dependents should migrate their specific use case.

name: sphinxcontrib-serializinghtml
remediation_notes: Small codebase (722 LOC) spread across many niche packages with no dominant user. Projects needing JSON/pickle Sphinx output could inline the serialization logic directly, reducing supply-chain risk from this dormant extension.

name: google-api-core
remediation_notes: Archived with code moved to google-cloud-python monorepo. Google recommends migrating to the relevant google-cloud-* package (e.g., google-cloud-storage) instead of using google-api-core directly.

name: oauth2client
remediation_notes: Google officially deprecated this in favor of google-auth. Depending on your integration (GCP, Gmail, Sheets), may also need google-api-python-client or google-cloud-python.

name: sphinxcontrib-htmlhelp
remediation_notes: Switch to Sphinx's native htmlhelp builder. Distributed across 21,968 small repositories with no dominant consumer; each project can migrate independently during routine documentation tooling updates.

name: jupyterlab-pygments
remediation_notes: The package is just 11 lines of Python providing CSS variable mappings for Pygments syntax highlighting. Dependents should copy this trivial code into their own codebase rather than maintain a dependency on unmaintained infrastructure.

name: sphinxcontrib-qthelp
remediation_notes: Niche Sphinx extension for Qt documentation (310 lines, zero dependencies). Dormant but working; QtHelp output has no maintained alternative. Pin the version and carry the low risk.

name: sphinxcontrib-devhelp
remediation_notes: No runtime dependencies and small codebase make this safe to pin. Most dependents can use Sphinx's default HTML output instead; projects requiring Devhelp format can easily fork the small extension if needed.

name: sphinxcontrib-applehelp
remediation_notes: This Sphinx extension hasn't been updated in 638 days but is stable—Apple Help format doesn't change. With usage split across 155 packages and 21k repos, ecosystem-wide remediation is impractical. Dependents should pin the version and report issues if Apple Help output needs fixes.

name: rfc3986
remediation_notes: Stable RFC 3986 implementation for strict URI validation. Dependents need RFC compliance beyond stdlib urllib.parse. High fork cost across 19k repos. Alternatives lack pure RFC compliance. Pin version and accept the risk.

name: docker
remediation_notes: No alternative covers Docker Engine API comprehensively. Pin to a stable version and monitor for security; dormancy is acceptable risk for mature infrastructure.

name: python-slugify
remediation_notes: Only 921 LOC and well-tested; copying into projects is feasible. Alternatively, fork and maintain if community coordination emerges.

name: flask-sqlalchemy
remediation_notes: Flask-SQLAlchemy is dormant but maintained through the Pallets Community Ecosystem; its dominant dependent (flask-session at 91.7% of usage) provides the usage anchor. Pin the version and rely on Pallets' institutional stewardship for critical issues.

name: google-cloud-storage
remediation_notes: Google's official Cloud Storage client, archived on GitHub but actively maintained in google-cloud-python monorepo with releases still shipping. Dependents should pin a recent version and keep using it.

name: commonmark
remediation_notes: The maintainer explicitly deprecated commonmark.py in the README and recommends markdown-it-py as a drop-in replacement for the CommonMark spec.

name: dataclasses
remediation_notes: This backport is obsolete: dataclasses has been in the Python standard library since 3.7 (2018). Remove this dependency and use the stdlib version instead—the API is identical. Python 3.6 is EOL; upgrade your minimum version if not already done.

name: google-resumable-media
remediation_notes: Google archived this repo and moved the code into the google-cloud-python monorepo. Dependents should update to use the maintained version from its new location.

name: isodate
remediation_notes: Stable, focused ISO 8601 parser with no runtime dependencies—pin the version and accept it. Those needing broader datetime support can evaluate python-dateutil, but for isolated date parsing the fixed version is safe and sufficient.

name: cached-property
remediation_notes: Replace with Python 3.8+ `functools.cached_property`—same API, no dependency, better maintained. Projects requiring Python 3.7 support can pin the last release (0.1.12).

name: httpcore
remediation_notes: Dormant (197d no commit, 369d no release) but not dead. 12k dependents across 250 packages with no clear steward. Pinning and monitoring for security is practical; codebase was well-tooled.

name: distro
remediation_notes: 923 lines with no dependencies make distro safe to vendor. Maintainer explicitly endorses vendoring; with 12k small dependents and no steward, this gives each consumer control.

name: mdurl
remediation_notes: mdurl is a small, stable URL utility for markdown parsing (~365 LOC, no runtime dependencies, straightforward code) distributed across 11,693 dependent repos with no dominant steward. At this size, vendoring the code directly is more practical than maintaining a separate package dependency.

name: funcsigs
remediation_notes: Backport of Python 3.3's built-in `inspect.signature()`. Python 2 EOL in 2020 makes this obsolete. Dependents on Python 3.3+ should use the standard library `inspect` module directly. Legacy Python 2 projects can vendor the 2.2K LOC if needed.

name: jeepney
remediation_notes: notify_py and sibling notification libraries account for 84% of usage and would inherit responsibility if jeepney breaks. No runtime dependencies means stable code poses minimal transitive risk; pin and carry.

name: backoff
remediation_notes: Copy the 2.5k LOC codebase into your project—it has no runtime dependencies and does one focused job. Alternatively, switch to the actively-maintained tenacity package if you prefer an external dependency.

name: google-crc32c
remediation_notes: CRC32C is a stable algorithm with no security updates needed. Pin to a recent wheel (3.9–3.14) for your platform and monitor for Python compatibility issues only. Archive status is not a problem.

name: flask-login
remediation_notes: Flask-login is small and stable with no maintained alternative. The 98.8% dependency concentration in flask-dance and ecosystem breadth make forking or replacement risky; pin the version and monitor for actual issues.

name: fqdn
remediation_notes: This 400-line FQDN validator is stable and self-contained. Dependents should copy the code into their projects and drop the dependency, or accept the pin if acquired transitively.

name: isoduration
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 5+ years but functionally stable; small surface (453 LOC, zero dependencies) makes inline adoption feasible for the scattered dependent base.

name: jsonpatch
remediation_notes: jsonpatch implements RFC 6902, a stable standard with no active vulnerabilities. Dormancy is acceptable for specifications that don't evolve; the dominant dependent (pyhf at 95.2%) can fork if modifications are ever needed.

name: overrides
remediation_notes: Small decorator library with no external dependencies. Safe to pin and use as-is. For new code on Python 3.12+, consider the built-in @override instead.

name: wtforms
remediation_notes: WTForms is dormant but foundational with no alternative—dependents should pin versions and be prepared to fork if needed, but wholesale replacement isn't realistic.

name: semver
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable with zero runtime dependencies. packaging.version is the maintained Python standard, though APIs differ (micro vs patch field naming, no bump methods). Accept and pin if migration effort is high.

name: pysocks
remediation_notes: Small, dependency-free protocol library suited for vendoring. Last commit 6.6 years ago but SOCKS protocol is stable and rarely needs changes. Most critical dependents are actively maintained and can absorb the code directly.

name: typing-inspect
remediation_notes: No maintained replacement exists for these type inspection utilities. Dependents should pin the version and carry the risk; large projects can evaluate vendoring if stability becomes critical.

name: dataclasses-json
remediation_notes: Dataclasses-json is dormant but stable. Pydantic is the actively maintained standard for Python data validation and JSON serialization; projects should plan migration to BaseModel for long-term support.

name: docker-pycreds
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 7+ years but implements a stable Docker credentials store API. The 267-line implementation is simple enough to vendor directly into projects that need it.

name: pytest-runner
remediation_notes: Archived and deprecated due to setup_requires security implications. Maintainers recommend removing pytest-runner from setup_requires and using tox or similar test tools instead.

name: google-cloud-bigquery
remediation_notes: Repository archived but code actively maintained in google-cloud-python monorepo; dependents can safely continue using this PyPI package with regular updates.

name: progressbar2
remediation_notes: Dormant progress library with 17 entry points distributed across 6090 repos; last release 608 days ago. Dependents should plan migration to tqdm (basic progress bars) or rich (advanced formatting) based on actual usage, since no single replacement covers all use cases.

name: rfc3339-validator
remediation_notes: This is 126 lines of pure Python with zero dependencies. Sentry and other dependents should copy the validation logic inline—it's small enough that the supply-chain risk outweighs the convenience of keeping the dependency.

name: monotonic
remediation_notes: This package is archived and explicitly deprecated in favor of Python's built-in `time.monotonic()` (available since 3.3). Analytics-python accounts for 90% of usage; almost all dependents can safely replace the import with the stdlib equivalent.

name: semantic-version
remediation_notes: Small, dependency-free library implementing a standard spec; 3+ years without commits suggests completeness. Pin to a known version, verify Python compatibility periodically, audit as needed.

name: humanfriendly
remediation_notes: humanfriendly is a grab-bag of terminal and text utilities (formatting, prompts, ANSI styling, size parsing). Different dependents use different slices—replace with focused alternatives like humanize for formatting, colorama/blessed for styling, inquirer for prompting, and pathlib for paths.

name: coloredlogs
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable; 5400+ dependent repos spread across 587 packages makes coordinated adoption infeasible. Pin the version. It performs a single job well with minimal maintenance burden.

name: rfc3986-validator
remediation_notes: Only 272 lines of Python with zero dependencies; unchanged since 2020. Dependents should vendor the validation code directly to eliminate a dormant dependency.

name: shellingham
remediation_notes: At 319 lines with zero dependencies, teams should copy this into their codebase. Shell detection is a utility most projects can own locally rather than maintain a dormant dependency for.

name: msrest
remediation_notes: Microsoft explicitly moved authentication to `azure-identity` and serialization to `azure-core`. Audit your usage and migrate to the appropriate replacement—most dependents will need both.

name: asynctest
remediation_notes: MMDet accounts for 90% of downstream usage. Migrate to pytest-asyncio, the actively maintained async testing standard for Python 3.8+, rather than forking or vendoring unmaintained code.

name: python-utils
remediation_notes: One dependent (django-utils2) accounts for 46% of usage; python-utils is small enough (3.6k LOC) to vendor into projects rather than maintain externally.

name: pytzdata
remediation_notes: dbnd accounts for 99.7% of real-world usage (122k downloads vs 155 for the next largest). The package is simple (942 Python LOC) but hasn't been updated since 2020, so timezone data is stale. dbnd should fork/maintain it or migrate to actively maintained tzdata package.

name: deprecation
remediation_notes: At 902 LOC with only a packaging dependency, dependents should copy this library into their codebase. The code is stable and focused enough to maintain independently.

name: ordered-set
remediation_notes: OrderedSet is stable and dependency-free with no maintained alternative. Pin the version and continue using it; for zero-dependency requirements, the 800-line implementation is small enough to vendor.

name: adal
remediation_notes: Microsoft archived ADAL in favor of MSAL with a published migration guide. Nearly all traffic flows through msrestazure; the ecosystem pressure is on Azure SDK maintainers to upgrade.

name: cachelib
remediation_notes: Flask-session accounts for nearly all usage. Cachelib is stable, dormant, and seeking maintainers via Pallets Ecosystem. Safe to pin in production.

name: flask-jwt-extended
remediation_notes: Dormant Flask JWT library with 2500+ dependents across projects. Since JWT is security-sensitive, migrate to an actively maintained alternative like authlib rather than pinning an unmaintained version.

name: annotated-types
remediation_notes: Dormant 2 years with no active maintainers, but simple stable code with zero dependencies used across 2,461 repos. One of the larger dependents should fork it or the community should establish a maintained fork; pinning versions works short-term but abandons Python compatibility maintenance.

name: msrestazure
remediation_notes: Microsoft officially deprecated this package; use azure-identity for authentication and azure-mgmt-core for management APIs. Top dependents are likely already migrated or will be via Azure SDK updates.

name: jaraco.classes
remediation_notes: Dormant since 758 days (no release), but recent commits show it's not abandoned. The small, stable codebase (781 LOC) is best handled by vendoring into your project.

name: msal-extensions
remediation_notes: msal-extensions provides MSAL token cache persistence via platform-specific keyrings. The maintained keyring library offers equivalent cross-platform keyring access; dependents can switch by combining keyring with MSAL's native SerializableTokenCache.

name: retry
remediation_notes: Tenacity is the actively maintained Python standard for retry logic with a compatible decorator API. Migration requires import and parameter adjustments.

name: cleo
remediation_notes: 98% of dependents are a single package. The 5799-LOC codebase is small enough to vendor for independence; most dependents can safely pin the current version while the v3 rewrite completes.

name: crashtest
remediation_notes: Unmaintained for 3.5 years with scattered small dependents and no clear steward. The codebase is small (624 LOC, no runtime deps) and suitable for vendoring rather than maintaining as an external dependency.

name: oscrypto
remediation_notes: Dormant for 4 years with 1,480 small dependents. Most should switch to cryptography, which is actively maintained and covers the same cryptographic operations.

name: pkgutil_resolve_name
remediation_notes: This 158-line backport can be vendored into projects needing Python <3.9 support, or dropped entirely by upgrading to Python 3.9+ and using pkgutil.resolve_name from the standard library.

name: sshtunnel
remediation_notes: Dormant but stable; pure Python with no transitive dependencies. Dagster-ssh dominates usage (85%); if long-term maintenance becomes critical, that project should consider forking.

name: pydata-google-auth
remediation_notes: Dormant wrapper around google-auth that's small enough (4.5k LOC) for dependents to inline; ibis-bigquery accounts for 82% of usage and could lead the migration.

name: applicationinsights
remediation_notes: Microsoft's legacy Application Insights SDK; the README directs to Azure SDK for Python's OpenTelemetry components. Azure tools dominating usage (87% in sfctl) should migrate to this maintained alternative.

name: analytics-python
remediation_notes: No releases in 4.8 years. Migrate to the officially maintained Segment analytics client; the top dependent (79% of usage) makes this transition practical.

name: flask-session
remediation_notes: Flask-Session provides stable, well-tested server-side session functionality. Dormancy is acceptable for mature infrastructure code; pin the version and monitor for security issues, though the Pallets Eco maintainers would likely respond to critical problems.

name: requests-aws4auth
remediation_notes: Provides AWS Signature v4 signing for requests. Small, stable codebase (2.7k LOC). Top dependent (pynessie) takes 42% of downloads; large dependents have the scale to adopt.

name: aws-requests-auth
remediation_notes: Nearly all usage concentrated in tidy3d. AWS SigV4 signing is built into boto3/botocore; switch to the official AWS SDK instead of pinning a dead third-party auth implementation.

name: sqlalchemy-jsonfield
remediation_notes: SQLAlchemy's native JSON type (available since 1.1, standard in 2.0+) handles cross-database JSON storage this package solved for. Since SQLAlchemy is already a runtime dependency, switching requires no new dependencies.

name: smdebug-rulesconfig
remediation_notes: AWS's SageMaker debugger rules config library. Dormant since ~2021 but stable—no dependencies and tight SageMaker coupling mean breaking changes are unlikely. Pin the version and accept the minimal risk; if sagemode stops working, AWS will fix it on their end.

name: click-man
remediation_notes: Focused utility with 829 LOC for converting Click CLI metadata to man pages. Simple enough for consuming projects to vendor directly rather than rely on the dormant package.

name: aiohappyeyeballs
remediation_notes: Implements happy eyeballs (RFC 8305) for async Python with no maintained alternative. Minimal dependent adoption (2 packages, 0 repos) and stable algorithm scope make pinning and accepting the maintenance risk the practical choice.
